transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’ve just been having a really hard time sitting still. Like in the radiology suite or in class, when I’m supposed to stay put, I start feeling like I’m crawling out of my skin. I’ve tried to just deal with it for months, and I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I still end up pacing, shifting around, or finding some reason to move. I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
Did this feeling of being unable to sit still start after you began a medication or changed the dose of one?
I don’t think so… I mean, not that I’ve noticed. I’m not sure if there’s something specific you’re thinking of, but I can’t really connect it to starting or changing a medication.
When you feel like you can’t sit still, do you also feel anxious or worried?

Not really anxious, I don’t think. I mean, I might get a little frustrated or embarrassed if I’m supposed to be sitting still and I can’t, but it doesn’t feel like I’m worrying about something specific. It’s more just this restless feeling, if that makes sense.
Did you have this same kind of trouble sitting still when you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I was a terrible kid or anything, but my parents still bring up elementary school conferences where teachers would say I was always out of my seat, or calling out, or kind of rushing ahead before the directions were even finished.

So… yeah, it was definitely happening way before middle school. It’s not just since I started radiology training.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people couldn’t?
No, I don’t think so. Like, I’ve never heard voices talking to me or seen things that other people weren’t seeing. At least nothing like that that I can think of.
Do you often have trouble paying attention, even when you’re trying to focus?
Um… I don’t think so, not in a major way. I mean, everyone zones out sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m constantly unable to pay attention when I’m trying. Unless you mean something specific by that?

Symptoms are not linked to medication change, are not primarily driven by anxiety, and there is no evidence of psychosis.
